title: Super Micro Computer Landed $60 Billion in Orders Last Quarter, but Trades at Just $30
detail:
Super Micro Computer Landed $60 Billion in Orders Last Quarter, but Trades at Just $30
Micah Zimmerman, The Motley Fool
Sun, August 9, 2026 at 5:50 AM EDT 4 min read
SMCI
NVDA
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) recently told investors something that would normally be considered great news. This producer of high-performance and high-efficiency computer servers said it booked more than $60 billion in new orders in a single quarter.

And yet the stock still trades around $30 per share. That disconnect between order book and valuation is what makes Supermicro (as it is also known) so interesting right now.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

In late July, Supermicro released a preliminary update for its fiscal fourth quarter (ended June 30) that focused almost entirely on demand and margins, not just headline revenue. Management said new orders during the quarter exceeded $60 billion, pushing its backlog to a record level as it closed out fiscal 2026.

Image source: Getty Images.

At the same time, Supermicro guided revenue to come in near the low end of its $11 billion to $12.5 billion-dollar range, but estimated gross margins of 15% to 17%, roughly double the 8.2% to 8.4% it had told investors to expect earlier. For a company that was not long ago seen as a lower-margin box builder, that is a very different story.

Massive server orders are coming in

Those orders are not just random server deals. In June, Supermicro announced that it had received huge AI server orders in recent weeks and laid out a plan to raise $7 billion through concurrent equity and equity-linked financing to fund the components needed to fulfill them. The company described this as part of its role as a "Total IT Solution Manufacturer for AI, Cloud, Storage, and 5G/Edge," essentially betting that being early and aggressive in AI infrastructure will matter more than short-term dilution.

To me, the combination of a $60 billion order wave and a financing package sized to meet it suggests customers are not just kicking the tires; they are committing real money to build AI data centers on Supermicro's designs.

So why does the stock still trade at roughly $30 instead of at some nosebleed AI multiple?

Part of the answer sits in the cautious language Supermicro uses in its own update. It explicitly notes that not all of those orders constitute firm commitments and that some may be subject to cancellation or delays. It also discloses that its board is overseeing an independent review of certain transactions related to alleged export control issues, and that its independent auditor has not yet reviewed the preliminary figures. Add in the large equity issuance needed to fund those orders, and you end up with real questions about how much of the current backlog will translate into high-margin, shareholder-friendly cash over time.

Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) is preparing to release fiscal fourth-quarter results on Aug. 11 after providing investors with an updated outlook that pointed to a backlog exceeding $60 billion, according to a previous company update.

Consensus estimates project Super Micro Computer will post earnings of $0.96 per share for the quarter, representing more than 124% growth from a year earlier. Revenue is expected to reach $11.55 billion, an increase of about 101% year over year.

Super Micro Computer said last month it now expects gross margin and adjusted gross margin in the range of 15% to 17%, improving from its earlier forecast of 8.2% to 8.4%. Wall Street analysts, however, remain watchful over the company's execution, cash flow trends and competitive pressures despite continued demand for artificial intelligence servers.

Ahead of Super Micro Computer's earnings release, according to GuruFocus ownership data, institutional investors owned 53.08% of Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ:SMCI) as of July 31, equivalent to about 343.37 million shares. Company insiders held 6.63%, or roughly 42.86 million shares.

GuruFocus data also showed that Chief Executive Charles Liang was the company's largest direct insider shareholder, holding about 40.43 million shares as of July 1.

PancakeSwap Expands Tokenized Equity Offerings with 10 New 'bStocks' on BNB Chain

Decentralized crypto exchange PancakeSwap (CRYPTO: $CAKE) expanded its tokenized equities offering on Thursday, listing 10 additional "bStocks" on BNB Chain to give users 24-hour access to shares of high profile companies ranging from semiconductor manufacturer ASML Holding to streaming powerhouse Netflix (NASDAQ: $NFLX).

The newly added BEP-20 tokens, which include Astera Labs, ASML Holding (NASDAQ: $ASML), AST SpaceMobile, Bitmine Immersion (NYSE: $BMNR), Coherent Corp, Credo Technology, IREN, Netflix, Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: $SMCI), and USA Rare Earth, are backed 1:1 by U.S. listed equity shares held at a regulated custodian. Issued by a Binance group affiliate, the tokens allow investors to maintain economic exposure to underlying stocks while bypassing traditional brokerage operating hours and settlement delays.

The expansion marks the latest phase in a broader push by PancakeSwap and BNB Chain to integrate real-world assets into decentralized finance (DeFi). Under the structure, token holders can verify collateral holdings daily, redeem positions fee free on Binance, or transfer tokens to self custodial wallets. Once on-chain, users can utilize the equity tokens across DeFi protocols for activities such as lending and liquidity provision.

PancakeSwap, one of the largest decentralized trading venues by volume, has progressively built out its stock terminal since launching bStocks in mid-June. The platform's effort reflects an accelerating race across the digital asset sector to capture market share in tokenized securities and composable finance.

Analysts note that while tokenized real-world assets offer enhanced liquidity and capital efficiency, they introduce distinct structural risks. bStocks do not grant voting rights or direct legal shareholder status in the underlying companies.

Furthermore, investors remain exposed to smart contract vulnerabilities, potential tracking errors relative to primary markets, and evolving regulatory frameworks across international jurisdictions.
